When authors incorporate esoteric concepts, such as the Kabbalah, into their narratives, it can be seen as a way to add depth and complexity to their storytelling.

  By tapping into archetypal structures, authors may be attempting to create a sense of universality and timelessness in their work, drawing on the collective unconscious to convey themes and ideas that resonate with readers on a deeper level.

  This can also be seen as a form of meta-commentary, where the author is commenting on the nature of reality, the human condition, and the role of storytelling itself.

  The use of esoteric concepts can also serve to create a sense of mystery and intrigue, inviting readers to engage with the narrative on a more intellectual and symbolic level.

  Some authors may be using these concepts as a way to explore the boundaries between reality and fantasy, or to challenge readers' perceptions of the world and their place in it.

  By incorporating esoteric elements, authors can create a sense of layers and depth in their work, inviting readers to uncover hidden meanings and interpretations.

  This can also be seen as a form of self-reflexivity, where the author is commenting on the nature of storytelling and the role of the reader in interpreting the narrative.

  Ultimately, the use of esoteric concepts in fiction can be seen as a way to create a richer, more nuanced, and more thought-provoking reading experience, one that rewards close attention and multiple readings.
